news.headline: 29-year-old techie falls from 30th floor of apartment, dies in Hyderabad: Police
news.story_lead: 29-year-old techie falls from 30th floor of apartment, dies in Hyderabad: Police A police officer at the Gachibowli police station said the deceased, a native of Telangana’s Suryapet district, worked for a Bengaluru-based IT firm A 29-year-old software engineer was found dead in the parking lot of a gated community in Hyderabad’s Nanakramguda late on Monday night, just two days after moving into the complex, police said. Investigators said the techie appeared to have died after falling from his 30th-floor rented apartment, but underlined that the circumstances surrounding the fatal fall remain under investigation. A police officer at the Gachibowli police station said the deceased, a native of Telangana’s Suryapet district, worked for a Bengaluru-based IT firm and moved into the apartment complex on Saturday.

Investigators said the techie appeared to have died after falling from his 30th-floor rented apartment, but underlined that the circumstances surrounding the fatal fall remain under investigation. A police officer at the Gachibowli police station said the deceased, a native of Telangana’s Suryapet district, worked for a Bengaluru-based IT firm and moved into the apartment complex on Saturday. “Late on Monday night, security guards spotted his body in the building’s parking area. He appears to have fallen from his floor and landed on a parked vehicle, suffering fatal injuries,” a senior police officer said. Security personnel immediately alerted residents, who rushed the victim to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Following a complaint filed by the victim’s cousin, the Gachibowli police have registered a case of suspicious death and transferred the body to Osmania General Hospital for an autopsy. Police suspect the techie died by suicide. “The exact cause and circumstances leading to the fall are under investigation. We are looking into all possibilities,” the officer added. news.story_lead: Kiran Bedi backs Jantar Mantar de-notification, explains why site is ‘least suited’ for protests Kiran Bedi had earlier called for protests to be restricted to Ramlila Ground, citing national security concerns amid demonstrations over NEET at Jantar Mantar. news.full_article_text: Kiran Bedi backs Jantar Mantar de-notification, explains why site is ‘least suited’ for protests Kiran Bedi had earlier called for protests to be restricted to Ramlila Ground, citing national security concerns amid demonstrations over NEET at Jantar Mantar. Former IPS officer Kiran Bedi has backed the decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, saying the location was ill-suited for demonstrations because of its narrow lanes and proximity to sensitive buildings and offices. In a post on X, Bedi said every city needed designated spaces for democratic expression, arguing that the administration had erred in choosing Jantar Mantar and failed to correct the decision earlier. Her remarks come after the Delhi Police, in an order issued on October 11, designated Ramlila Maidan, Burari Maidan and CBD Ground in Shahdara as alternative venues for protests. Also Read | Jantar Mantar in Lutyens’ Delhi de-notified as protest site; 3 new venues named ‘Every city requires an open space for democratic expression’ Deep Dive “During my lifetime of policing the city of Delhi, I have seen protest sites shift from the PM’s residence and Teen Murti Marg (then Mrs Gandhi’s residence) to the roads of Lutyens’ Delhi in the early 1970s, then to India Gate in the 1980s, and later to Jantar Mantar,” she wrote. “Every city requires an open space for democratic expression, which we also call a protest, but forgets to provide for,” she added. Bedi urged city planners to take note, arguing that Jantar Mantar was the least suited to serve as a protest site because of its narrow lanes, proximity to sensitive buildings and offices, and location near Connaught Place, a major commercial hub. “I think the administration of that time erred in taking that decision and did not correct it all this while. And the consequences are there to see,” she wrote. She said the Union home ministry had identified Ramlila Maidan and other locations for protests, adding that the shift perhaps required judicial intervention. “Now we need a clear security and functioning plan for Ramlila Maidan to be stated when according permissions,” Bedi added. Why Bedi wants protests shifted to Ramlila Ground Bedi had earlier also, in July, called for protests to be restricted to Ramlila Ground, citing national security concerns amid demonstrations over NEET at Jantar Mantar and the need to protect public spaces such as Connaught Place. She had called for restricting protest permissions to Ramlila Ground in an interview with ANI news agency. She argued that demonstrations should be held away from sensitive areas around Parliament and major commercial hubs. “The main reason is to keep protests away from the gates of Parliament House for national safety,” Bedi had said, advocating a more restrained and technology-driven approach to crowd management. She had argued that concentrating demonstrations at Ramlila Ground would help protect public spaces and prevent disruption or vandalism in commercial areas such as Connaught Place. Bedi had also called for changes in crowd management, suggesting that Civil Defence volunteers and women police personnel form the first and second lines of crowd control, rather than heavily armed police personnel being deployed at the outset. Riot police, she said, should be deployed only as a “last resort” and “strictly on a need basis”. In a separate post on X at the time, Bedi advocated deploying Civil Defence volunteers to manage student protests, describing them as the first line of defence, similar to the Border Security Force’s role along the country’s borders. In a video accompanying the post, she suggested that Civil Defence volunteers wearing protective gear but not carrying canes should face protesters. Riot police, meanwhile, should be responsible for protecting the volunteers and preventing violence or damage to public property. Bedi's remarks had come amid criticism of security forces' actions against protestors who participated in the July 20 Cockroach Janta Party-led protest march to Parliament. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Priyanjali Narayan Priyanjali Narayan is a journalist with Hindustan Times based in New Delhi. The Harvard Club of India, the official alumni group of the United States' prestigious Harvard University alumni in India, clarified on Monday that it did not endorse or issue any statement regarding the ongoing protests in Delhi. The club was referring to a letter reportedly issued by 100 Harvard University alumni condemning "police brutality, unlawful detention, and violations of constitutional rights of all peaceful protestors" in Delhi during the protest held on October 10 against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision exercise. However, the club on Monday distanced itself from the reported letter and said that the statement did not represent the organisation's official position. Rajat Sethi, a member of the club's Executive Committee, told news agency ANI that some Harvard University alumni had issued the letter without representing the organisation. He said the clarification was necessary because the club had not issued or endorsed any statement on the protests or the detentions that followed. “As a member of the elected body of the Executive Council of the Harvard Club of India, which is the official alumni group of Harvard University alumni in India, I wanted to issue a clarification that certain individuals have gone ahead and issued a letter remarking on and making comments about the recent protest and the detention that followed. I wanted to issue a clarification that this is not the official position of the Harvard Club of India,” Sethi said. Also read: Supreme Court flags 14 'defects' in Rahul Gandhi's petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar He added that the club's charter and mandate do not permit it to issue political statements either in its own name or on behalf of Harvard University. “Therefore, this clarification is to explain to the larger audience that certain individuals who happen to be alumni of Harvard University have issued the statement in their personal capacity. While we respect personal expression, that is not a substitute for institutional representation,” he said. news.full_article_text: Three-day BRICS Theatre Festival begins in Delhi, India showcases 'Samudra Manthan' New Delhi, The three-day BRICS Theatre Festival began at the National School of Drama here on Monday, bringing together theatre practitioners, scholars, students and cultural representatives from nine BRICS member and partner countries. The festival will feature performances from national theatre schools and leading theatre institutions from participating countries - India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Iran, Vietnam, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia. The festival's performances will be staged at venues across New Delhi, including NSD's Abhimanch and Sammukh auditoriums, Kamani Auditorium, LTG Auditorium and Meghdoot Theatre, and tickets can be purchased through BookMyShow for ₹ 200 each. The inaugural day featured the play 'Samudra Manthan', written by Asif Ali, with design, direction and music by the director of the NSD. The play was staged at the Abhimanch Auditorium on the NSD premises. Organised by the Ministry of Culture, the festival provides a platform for artistic and cultural exchange through the shared language of theatre, the culture ministry said in a statement. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat was present at the opening ceremony as the chief guest. The ceremony was also attended by Union Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal; Secretary , Ministry of External Affairs, Sudhakar Dalela, who was India's BRICS Sherpa for 2026; and Chittaranjan Tripathy, NSD's director. Ambassadors and Heads of Mission from various participating countries were also present at the inaugural ceremony, it said. news.headline: Prices of pulses soar amid supply crunch and adverse weather
news.story_lead: Prices of pulses soar amid supply crunch and adverse weather Adverse weather, lower supplies and costlier imports are lifting Indian pulse prices, with pigeon pea nearing 2023-24 highs. Pigeon pea ( arhar ) prices are moving towards their 2023-24 highs, when retail prices crossed ₹ 200 per kg, as adverse weather, lower supplies and rising import costs push up prices, according to a report by the India Pulses and Grains Association (IPGA). This rise in prices is also being witnessed in other pulses such as black gram and chickpeas as domestic production is expected to fall and a falling rupee is seen pushing up import costs.
news.full_article_text: Prices of pulses soar amid supply crunch and adverse weather Adverse weather, lower supplies and costlier imports are lifting Indian pulse prices, with pigeon pea nearing 2023-24 highs. Pigeon pea ( arhar ) prices are moving towards their 2023-24 highs, when retail prices crossed ₹ 200 per kg, as adverse weather, lower supplies and rising import costs push up prices, according to a report by the India Pulses and Grains Association (IPGA). This rise in prices is also being witnessed in other pulses such as black gram and chickpeas as domestic production is expected to fall and a falling rupee is seen pushing up import costs. Wholesale pigeon pea prices rose sharply in the last week. Prices in the key market of Akola, Maharashtra were ₹ 108-108.25 per kg. In Gulbarga region of Karnataka, they reached ₹ 103-113 per kg. Prices in these markets rose by ₹ 17-19 per kg over the past month in some cases, according to the IPGA data. The latest rally comes amid concerns over the kharif pigeon pea crop in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, where adverse weather and dry conditions have affected crop prospects. The national average retail price of pigeon pea stood at ₹ 127.90 per kg on October 11, according to the Department of Consumer Affairs. Black gram prices have also risen because of limited supplies from Myanmar, higher export offers and delays in shipments through Chennai port. The IPGA said congestion had delayed vessel berthing and reduced stocks available for immediate delivery. Imported Myanmar fair average quality (FAQ) black gram was quoted at ₹ 101 per kg in Delhi on October 10, up from ₹ 88.75 a month earlier. Domestic black gram prices have increased despite fresh arrivals. According to IPGA, around 60-70% of the new crop arrivals have been of poor to average quality, causing prices to rise. Meanwhile, chickpea prices are also showing an uptick ahead of the rabi sowing season, supported by buying from traders and mills, festival demand for dal and gram flour, and lower arrivals. Pressure may rise in coming months as the next crop outlook remains uncertain. In Maharashtra and Karnataka, low soil moisture and deficient rainfall could affect chickpea sowing. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Pallavi Singhal Pallavi Singhal covers agriculture, food policy and the rural economy from New Delhi. news.story_lead: Iran security chief speaks to NSA Ajit Doval on call, discusses ‘issues of mutual interest’ The two leaders exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and his Iranian counterpart Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional and international developments and bilateral ties on Monday against the backdrop of a flare-up in hostilities in West Asia. India has maintained a delicate balance in its ties with Iran and key players in West Asia, urging for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to end the conflict and opposing all attacks on merchant shipping and civilian infrastructure.
news.full_article_text: Iran security chief speaks to NSA Ajit Doval on call, discusses ‘issues of mutual interest’ The two leaders exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and his Iranian counterpart Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional and international developments and bilateral ties on Monday against the backdrop of a flare-up in hostilities in West Asia. India has maintained a delicate balance in its ties with Iran and key players in West Asia, urging for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to end the conflict and opposing all attacks on merchant shipping and civilian infrastructure. Rezaei, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of Iran, held a phone conversation with Doval and exchanged views on the “latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries”, the Iranian embassy said on social media without giving details. There was no readout on the conversation from the Indian side. The conversation came two days after an Indian national was killed and 10 others injured in an attack on the international airport in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh by Iran-backed Houthi rebels, and a day after attacks on two merchant vessels with Indian crew members near the Strait of Hormuz. Two Indian seafarers were reported missing after a drone attack on MT Petrol Dolphin. During a meeting on the margins of the Brics Summit in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian to resolve the West Asia conflict through dialogue, and sought continued efforts to ensure freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers. The two leaders discussed recent developments in West Asia, and the external affairs ministry said in a readout that Modi reiterated India’s “consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy”. The Indian side has grappled with striking a balance between its historic ties with Iran and its expressions of solidarity with Gulf Arab states, which have repeatedly been targeted by the Iranian military for housing US military bases. The Indian side has also been irked by Iranian attacks on merchant vessels near the Strait of Hormuz that have killed and injured Indian seafarers. Eleven seafarers are among the 18 Indians killed so far in the West Asia conflict, which was triggered by attacks by Israel and the US on Iran in February. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports about just how warm the fridges and freezers could become in that process. Danfoss said the affected cold units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a risk they had identified. The firm added in s statement that it had "long advised" businesses to keep supported systems up to date. "Reliable refrigeration is critical to our customers' operations, and we remain committed to supporting our customers and helping them maintain secure and reliable systems they are used to." The full scale of the attack is unclear, but figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 400 stores were affected out of 15,000 or so overall in France. Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed. In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group - which owns IntermarchÃ© and Netto - said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon. The stores had "taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units", it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves "as soon as possible". news.full_article_text: Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday - Published 12 October 2026, 07:42 BST Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.full_article_text: ‘Pause SIR, hold independent audit of voter deletion’: INDIA bloc petition to Supreme Court lists 10 requests The petition raises concerns over the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise” of the election body's collective powers by CEC during the ongoing SIR. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, along with 10 INDIA bloc leaders, filed a petition in the Supreme Court on Monday against the Election Commission of India (ECI) on issues linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and alleged poll irregularities. As Gandhi could not reach the Supreme Court to file the petition in person, his advocate, S Prasanna, filed it, naming the ECI, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, and the two other election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, as respondents. What the INDIA bloc petition says The petition raises concerns over the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise” of the election body's collective powers by CEC Gyanesh Kumar during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the integrity of the electoral process, and the alleged infringement of eligible citizens’ constitutional right to register as voters and exercise their right to vote. Here are the key points: Suspend ongoing SIR until the issues raised are considered Deep Dive It directs the ECI to suspend the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across the States of the Union until the issues raised in the petition are considered and decided, to protect the rights of eligible voters and preserve the integrity of the electoral process. Petition seeks SIR decision records, ECINET and ERONET access logs The petition seeks a directive to the Election Commission of India (ECI) to place on record the complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections relating to each disputed decision concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. It also seeks the relevant ECINET and ERONET access logs and the complete file recording the decision dated June 24, 2025, to commence the SIR across the country, in furtherance of the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19 and 21, read with Article 324 of the Constitution of India. Review SIR decisions under Article 324 and relevant law The petition seeks a review of whether the disputed SIR decisions comply with Article 324 of the Constitution, Section 18 of the 2023 Act governing the Election Commissioners, and the Supreme Court’s ruling in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India. It also seeks to have any decisions found to be unlawful quashed or set aside. Action against those responsible The petition also seeks against those responsible for violating the constitutional or statutory provisions governing the preparation and revision of electoral rolls, including Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. ECI decisions on SIR to be recorded The petition also seeks a direction to the Election Commission to ensure that every decision of the Election Commission relating to the Special Intensive Revision is taken and duly minuted in accordance with Section 18 of the 2023 Act. Ensure compliance of Form 6 with prescribed rules The petition directs the commission to ensure that the online Form 6 conforms to the form prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, unless and until the said Rules are lawfully amended in accordance with the applicable procedure. Constitute independent committee The petition also seeks the constitution of an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with technical experts and other eminent citizens, to audit voter deletions and modifications during the SIR, as well as access to and changes made to electoral-roll databases, including ECINET and ERONET. It further seeks a review of decisions, policies, procedures and technical systems relating to Electronic Voting Machines, in line with global best practices to ensure free and fair elections. Directive to issue booth-wise list of deleted voters, reasons for deletion and restoration The petition also seeks the election commission to publish booth-wise lists of all voters deleted during the SIR, along with the reasons for each deletion and a gender- and age-wise breakdown, and to provide an effective mechanism for restoring the names of eligible voters to the electoral rolls. Notice before voter deletions, inclusion deadline for eligible voters in poll-bound states The petition further seeks a direction that no voter’s name be deleted from the electoral rolls without prior notice and a reasonable opportunity of hearing in accordance with law. It also seeks to ensure that eligible persons in Punjab and other poll-bound states are permitted to apply for inclusion in the electoral rolls until the last date allowed by law. Petition seeks any other relief to protect electoral integrity and voting rights Lastly, it is prayed that this court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case, in order to protect the integrity of the electoral process and the right of every eligible citizen to vote. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world.
